Medicare growth and primary care capacity by county

2,843 U.S. counties, 2014–2023. Medicare enrollment growth set against primary care physicians per 1,000 adults 65 and older. Select a county for details.

Select a county on the map to see its older population, physician capacity, shortage designation and trajectory group.

Groups. Fast growth is the top third of counties by growth in Medicare beneficiaries (above 19.4%, 2014–15 to 2022–23). Low capacity is the bottom third by physicians per 1,000 adults 65+ (below 1.30 in 2022–23). Trajectory clusters come from optimal matching of unsmoothed yearly states, 2015–2023.

Counties not in the study (gray) have fewer than 1,000 Medicare beneficiaries in 2014, incomplete data, or are in Connecticut or Alaska, where county geographies changed. Hawaii and Alaska are shown for context only.

Data used.

  • CMS Medicare Geographic Variation Public Use File, county level, 2014–2024: total Medicare beneficiaries (growth) and Medicare Advantage participation.
  • HRSA Area Health Resources File, six county releases (2019-20 to 2024-25): primary care physicians, nurse practitioners and physician assistants (National Provider Identifier registry, all specialties), primary care shortage designations (2025), and the 2023 USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Code.
  • Census Bureau 2010–2020 intercensal county estimates by age and sex (CC-EST2020INT-AGESEX-ALL): population 65 and older, 2014–2019.
  • Census Bureau Vintage 2025 county estimates by age and sex (CC-EST2025-AGESEX-ALL): population 65 and older, 2020–2023.
  • Census Bureau county total populations, 2010–2020 intercensal (CO-EST2020INT-POP) and Vintage 2025 (CO-EST2025-POP): used to check the Area Health Resources File series, not shown on the map.
  • American Community Survey 2019–2023 5-year table S1810: share of adults 65 and older with a disability or an ambulatory difficulty (a proxy for need, not a frailty measure; civilian noninstitutionalized population).
  • 2010 Census cartographic boundary file, counties, 1:500,000: map geometry.

Nurse practitioner and physician assistant counts cover all specialties. Descriptive results, no causal claims.
